title: prevent-admission-collapse-during-sustained-mixed-context-waves
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported recurring high tail latency and intermittent request starvation under sustained mixed-length traffic waves (short chat messages + sporadic very long context requests). Incidents manifest as abrupt admission collapse: small low-latency requests are delayed for seconds when the batcher is occupied by long-context inflight windows and prefetch activity, followed by KV cache thrashing and eviction storms.

Observed behavior: Under a sustained wave with 5-10% long-context requests (>= 32k tokens effective), the continuous batcher opens large admission windows and prefetches KV pages aggressively. This causes two interacting failures: (1) admission reservoir is drained by long inflight windows causing short requests to queue and starve, and (2) KV cache eviction hysteresis is too aggressive, triggering thrashing which increases service cpu/gpu stalls and furthering tail amplification. Symptoms reported: 95th/99th token latency spikes, customer errors in Private due to upgrade window interference, and Dedicated tenants seeing throughput collapse during maintenance windows.

Repro steps (internal lab): 1) Use workload generator with mixed distribution: 90% short (<= 512 tokens), 10% long (>= 16k token effective) spaced at Poisson arrivals. 2) Route to canary host with continuous-batcher enabled and KV cache size tuned to 70% nominal. 3) Observe admission window growth, then small-request queue build-up, followed by KV eviction rate increase and token-latency surge. Repro is reliable in ~10-15 minutes when prefetch enabled and admission smoothing disabled.

Root cause hypothesis: The batcher admission logic treats inflight long-context windows as first-class citizens without enforcing a short-request protection quota. Prefetch logic eagerly reserves cache slots and triggers eviction when windows overlap across concurrent long requests. Additionally, the admission expiry and reservoir replenishment math does not account for long-lived inflight leases, allowing admission credit to be effectively stolen by a small number of long-context flows.

Proposed fix: 1) Implement shortflow-velocity guard: reserve a small guaranteed admission quota (configurable per-host and tenant) that cannot be consumed by long inflight windows. 2) Add admission lease TTL and transparent expiry (timebound prefetched reservation) to prevent immortalized leases from starving others. 3) Introduce KV eviction hysteresis + grace window: prefetch reservations should not immediately evict live cache lines until cache pressure crosses a higher threshold; older prefetched entries should be deprioritized for eviction. 4) Preferential de-prioritization: when a mixed-length wave is detected, we shrink admission windows for long-context requests using progressive backoff while preserving short-request single-token latency SLO. 5) Add tenant-level microquotas for Dedicated to prevent one tenant's long flows from collapsing host-level admission.

Testing plan: Unit tests for admission TTL and quota enforcement. Integration test with workload generator to validate small-request tail latency remains within 2x baseline under mixed workload. Chaos test: simulate maintenance window + prefetch wave to confirm no regression. Canary rollout with step-scaling 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% across Hosted; Dedicated scheduled canary on reserved pool; Private customers given opt-in Kubernetes chart with feature flag.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag and host-level knobs. 2) Canary rollout in Hosted (small region), monitor token-latency, admission metrics, kv_eviction_rate, cache_hit_ratio. 3) If stable for 72h, widen. For Dedicated/Private, ship as opt-in patch and coordinate with affected customers (on-call SRE to be present).

Monitoring & Alerts: New alerts for admission_credit_depletion_rate, shortflow_queue_growth (>50 ms sustained), kv_eviction_spike (>200 ev/s sustained). Add dashboards: admission-credit heatmap, per-tenant admission-utilization, prefetch-reservation-count. Postmortem artifacts will be linked on the ticket.

Stakeholders: PM: Lina Rodriguez; Design (console): Arjun Singh (for telemetry surface); SRE: Priya Nair; Affected customers: Acme Health (Private), NovaSearch (Dedicated), and an internal Hosted sandbox customer used for repro.

Deliverables: PR for runtime admission quota + TTL, PR for kv eviction hysteresis, updated canary runbook, integration test harness, and release notes for Dedicated/Private packaging.

2026-03-01 - Owen Patel: Hypothesis refined: admission leases never expire if prefetch handshake fails; added short-term patch to enforce 10s lease TTL as hotfix. Deployed hotfix to Hosted canary; observed short-tail latency restore from 2.1s->120ms in canary region. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148

2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (SRE): Hotfix mitigated immediate customer impact for Hosted. Dedicated customers still exposed during maintenance windows. Recommended implementing tenant microquota and KV hysteresis before widescale rollout.

2026-03-06 - Owen Patel: Began work on admission quota + graceful backoff. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-43210+Admission+Quota+Design. Added unit tests and integration harness. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2189 (WIP).

2026-03-09 - Lina Rodriguez (PM): Coordinating Dedicated customer communication and Private upgrade schedule. Requesting runbook and rollback plan for 1% -> 25% canary. Added "customer-comm" label and asked for playbook entries.
